# h3_eips (Data Source)

Lists the Elastic IPs of a project, optionally only free (`bound = false`) or only bound ones. This is the Terraform side of the console's EIP selector: pick a free address and pass it to `eip_id`. The list is read at plan time; two configurations picking `ids[0]` of the same pool can race, in which case the second apply fails with `EIP_ALREADY_BOUND` and nothing is changed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The console's EIP selector in Terraform: take a free address of the project
# pool instead of leasing a new one.
data "h3_eips" "free" {
  bound = false
}

resource "h3_database" "app" {
  name     = "app"
  engine   = "postgres"
  cpu      = 1
  memory   = "2Gi"
  size     = "10Gi"
  white_ip = true
  eip_id   = data.h3_eips.free.ids[0]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `bound` (Boolean) `false`: only free EIPs; `true`: only bound ones; unset: all
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (UUID); the provider default when omitted

### Read-Only

- `eips` (Attributes List) EIPs, sorted by name (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--eips))
- `ids` (List of String) EIP IDs, sorted by name

<a id="nestedatt--eips"></a>
### Nested Schema for `eips`

Read-Only:

- `bound` (Boolean) Attached or reserved
- `bound_resource_id` (String) ID of the bound resource
- `bound_resource_type` (String) Type of the bound resource
- `description` (String) EIP comment (null when not set)
- `id` (String) EIP ID
- `ip_address` (String) Public IPv4 address
- `name` (String) EIP name
- `status` (String) EIP status
